answer.evidence: The width profile of the cap is 7, 11, 11, then 13 for rows 4-7, and then it drops straight to the 7-wide shaft at row 8. It is rounded only at its upper edge and has a flat bottom sitting directly on the shaft, so it is a dome or hat, not an ellipse plate. Rows 6-7 are a teal underside strip, which is a vertical face and not a top surface. No back-and-front rim ellipse is visible. The shaft (rows 8-26) and base (rows 27-30) are drawn as vertical faces with no horizontal top. The object therefore reads as a front elevation.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a small bollard-style sign with a cylindrical grey body, a dome cap and a yellow number plate. It shows about 4 lightness steps on the body (highlight, light, mid, dark) plus the plate. The measured facts show 12 visible tones per tile, equal to kiosk-a and above bus-shelter-a (6), though below vending-a (20). Near-flat coverage is 0%, and 0% of the dark edge pixels are neutral, so the outline leans toward a tint rather than black. The piece is thin and small, so the per-tile density fact is not held against it. By eye, the body shading is clean but fairly simple, and the surface has little grain. It sits at the level of bus-shelter-a and kiosk-a but is not richer than them. It would be accepted next to those references, though the shallow ramp and sparse texture leave it a little thinner than the vending machine.
